claims.author: maflcko
claims.harm: modifying core consensus/node miner logic in src/node to accommodate test-only mining behavior introduces dead code and maintenance burden
claims.quote: Generally, I am not sure about modifying real code to accommodate test-only code. It would be better to not modify `src/node` at all and just put the test-only code in the test-only code paths.

status_by.quote: Tried to follow your approach, actually it makes things easier :)

claims.status_note: addressed by moving logic away from src/node

claims.author: andrewtoth
claims.harm: adding a new generatetomany RPC incurs code bloat, extra test maintenance, and deprecation cycles when extending generateblock is more flexible and fixes reward fee issues
claims.quote: New RPCs require adding more code to test, and once added must go through a deprecation cycle to be removed (if they can be removed at all without disrupting too many users).

status_by.quote: Squashed all commits and removed the first approach (`generatetomany`)

claims.status_note: author removed generatetomany and squashed commits

claims.author: mzumsande
claims.question: asks for the motivation to be documented on GitHub rather than requiring readers to check Twitter
claims.quote: Could the motivation be added here? Doesn't seem ok having to resort to twitter (where people without an account can't even see most of the thread) to know the reason for a PR.

status_by.quote: Here is my motivation: When mining a block on regtest, the command "generatetoaddress" is available if you want to send the entire coinbase to 1 address.

claims.status_note: supertestnet provided the motivation directly in the thread

claims.author: maflcko
claims.quote: not sure about forcing an array, when all tests mostly just want to provide a single dummy value. it would be good to make this optional and then, require one of `output` or `outputs` to be present, or maybe even fallback to `OP_TRUE` if none are given?
claims.request: make output/outputs optional and fallback to OP_RETURN if none are provided

status_by.quote: OP_RETURN fallback if no address or descriptor set is provided.

claims.author: naiyoma
claims.question: are you planning to add generatetomany and also extend generateblock, or keep only one approach?
claims.quote: I'm a bit confused about the current approach. Are you planning to add `generatetomany` and also extend `generateblock` to accommodate an array of addresses?

status_by.quote: `generatetomany` will not be added. I have to delete that code.

claims.status_note: author confirmed generatetomany would be removed

claims.author: maflcko
claims.quote: I am also thinking about splitting up the "make this arg optional". Seems like a small and easy preparatory pull request?
claims.request: split up making the argument optional into a preparatory pull request

claims.author: achow101
claims.quote: Why? I think it would be simpler to just require that at least one output address/descriptor is specified.
claims.request: require at least one output address/descriptor instead of allowing an empty list

claims.author: achow101
claims.harm: requiring an array rather than continuing to accept a string breaks backwards compatibility for scripts and automated tests using generateblock
claims.quote: Although this RPC is only used by tests, I don't think we should be breaking backwards compatibility here. It's equally easy to determine whether this parameter is a string, so we can accept a string
claims.status_note: added backwards compatibility support for string argument

claims.author: andrewtoth
claims.harm: omitting the transaction parameter in existing functional tests changes their behavior to mine the mempool instead of generating empty blocks
claims.quote: Otherwise this should be backwards compatible, and mining the mempool instead of an empty block can be a behavior change in the tests.

status_by.quote: I will add back the `transactions=[]` you are right that is a behavior change and this PR should not be changing that. T

claims.author: sedited
claims.question: asks whether custom split rewards are supposed to be implemented in this PR
claims.quote: Is this supposed to be implemented here now?

status_by.quote: As mentioned before https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32468#issuecomment-2965555591, I think this PR is good as is and custom rewards split can be implemented in a follow-up PR.

claims.status_note: author answered that it could be a follow-up or included if required

claims.author: stickies-v
claims.harm: limiting the RPC interface to equal splits rather than supporting custom reward amounts handicaps its usefulness for the sake of CLI convenience
claims.quote: Custom rewards are the general solution, why not just implement that right away? It's useful to keep the CLI commands ergonomic, but I think it's a mistake to handicap the RPC interface just to make C

status_by.quote: Bicaru20 implemented the custom split rewards.

claims.author: stickies-v
claims.quote: It also looks like this work should be split up in multiple commits, I think the `outputs` changes and the mempool changes are orthogonal?
claims.request: split up the PR into multiple commits for outputs changes and mempool changes

status_by.quote: Working on it. Idk why I structured it so bad in the first place 😅

claims.status_note: author agreed and worked on commit structure
